mentl/d273f97:
The previous pin bisected a trap to "a state initializer cannot read its
config" across four wheel-scale marches. A 30-line fixture reproduces it
in two seconds, and splitting it pins the boundary exactly: handler
h(start) with n = start runs and answers 10; with n = start + 1 traps.
Direct assignment survives only because lower_state_init special-cases a
bare config VarRef structurally into LUpval(0, slot), needing no binding
at all. Anything larger needs the name to resolve, and it does not.

The emitted WAT names its own root: unbound name start, infer proved it
missing, the lowering will not guess it into a global. The lowering is
correct and refusing to fabricate. The other half is in infer: both
HandlerDeclStmt sites reach register_handler, which checks state-field
names against op names, mints config tparams, env_extends the handler,
and never walks a single init expression. The only infer_expr over a
state init in the file is for resume-with updates.

So the class is bigger than the peer it explains. Everything in a with
field = init clause is unjudged — no types, no name resolution, no
diagnostics. It has never bitten because every init the wheel writes is
a literal, a nullary call, or a bare config ref.

And it is a silent wrong. mentl check reports nothing on the trapping
program, then it exits 134. The MissingName floor's own comment expects
infer to have fired a precise spanned E_MissingVariable first, and for
ordinary code it does; here infer never walked the expression, so
nothing fired and the executable gate had nothing to refuse.

Not built deliberately. The fix is one change for both halves — infer
judges decl-side state inits with config params in scope — and its blast
radius is real: expressions the wheel has never judged become judged.
The fixture stays a repro rather than a gate, because gating today's
behaviour green would canonize the bug.

mentl/d242b24:
Convert the two largest same-file string builders to stream through the
WasmOut effect handler directly. Each item is printed immediately via out()

sonido/d20a708:
Checkpoint B: wire the dormant MacroMap<6> into the standalone editor as a
performance surface, mapping toward the pedal's six knobs.

- Right-click any param knob/combo → "Map to Macro 1–6 / Clear". The menu lives
  in gui-core (new widgets/param_menu.rs) so the plugin reuses it; the chosen
  action is surfaced through egui temp-data and drained once per frame by the
  app, keeping gui-core decoupled from the host's macro map.
- Mount the live K1–K6 macro row beside the morph band in one full-width
  "performance" panel (graph mode) — the two control clusters that map to the
  pedal. Turning a macro sweeps every mapped param at once.
- The GUI owns the map and applies it straight through the bridge on macro move
  (the audio thread reads the bridge as always, so a macro move is just a
  batched param write — no audio-thread changes, no SetMacroMap command). Range
  + curve come from each param's descriptor (log for freq, snap for stepped).
- Binding is exclusive (a param drives at most one macro) via new
  MacroMap::clear_target; binding does not yank the param — it keeps its value
  until the macro is next moved (last-writer-wins with direct edits).
- Click a macro's name → floating mapping editor: rename (names map to physical
  knobs), review/remove the params it drives, clear all.
- Globals (input/master gain, morph position) route through apply_global so a
  macro can drive the whole-rig morph; morph-speed awaits the morph band's speed
  knob (Workstream C).

Known limit: mappings are slot-index-keyed, so reordering effects can point a
macro at a different slot — fixed by stable effect UIDs (Workstream A). Out-of-
range targets are safe no-ops. Macros are in-memory (session persistence lands
with the patch format).
